So in our case there isn’t that much benefit of this proposal, but generally it makes sense, especially for clients that are more disk based. this isn't kept in memory, you may need to recover pretty old states to perform a state transition You could be syncing a very old chain to regenerate a state to serve some beacon chain data from a past state. you could be syncing a live block from a peer after 3 weeks not finalizing etc. yea, for older blocks it's an issue. would be much easier if those new fields would be part of beacon block but this envelope proposal kinda makes it something close to a part of beacon block

excerpts.author: sauliusgrigaitis
excerpts.content: But this data isn’t big and can be kept in memory?

excerpts.author: sauliusgrigaitis
excerpts.content: So Grandine tries to keep in memory all the information it needs for the unfinalised part of the chain (it gets a bit more tricky when non-finalisation starts), so in our case we would just store new Electra specific data in-memory. So in our case there isn’t that much benefit of this proposal, but generally it makes sense, especially for clients that are more disk based.
